A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same prior-based text filtering work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including the image-based examples added in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original pretraining and downstream evaluation results on Dolma and Pile-GitHub, alongside filtering analyses and ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds FastText comparisons, scaling experiments, Turkish mixture tests, and MMLU-Pro retention results.

M1.justification: The token-frequency priors, document mean and standard deviation, median-distance filtering, and combined selection procedure remain unchanged. The standard-deviation-only and blended-corpus variants in v3 Appendix D.1 already appeared in v1 Appendix B.1.1.

E1.justification: v3 adds Turkish-English mixtures (Table 4) and MMLU-Pro questions injected into Dolma for retention evaluation (Table 12), extending coverage to an agglutinative language and preservation of complex-question data. The original corpora and downstream benchmarks remain. MMLU-Pro is used for filtering analysis, not downstream reasoning-accuracy evaluation.

E2.justification: FastText is added to the main Dolma comparison at both model sizes in Table 2. Its qualitative case study already existed in v1, but these downstream comparisons did not. The other comparators remain; v3's vanilla Dolma matches v1's no-filter baseline.

E3.justification: Section 4.1.1 adds Qwen2.5-3B and 1.5B evaluations extending training to 12B tokens. v3 also introduces a 25% selection-threshold experiment and a benchmark-injection protocol measuring MMLU-Pro retention across thresholds. These are additional evaluation settings; the original main experiments retain their reported settings.

E4.justification: v3 adds Turkish generalization tests, the 25% threshold ablation, MMLU-Pro preservation analysis, and expanded ranked outlier examples in Appendix J. Conversely, v1 Table 6's cross-tokenizer outlier-overlap analysis is removed. Existing rare-term, blended-prior, block-size, and prior-PPL correlation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Token-prior standard deviations and twofold training-data repetition are not uncertainty estimates for experimental results.

E6.justification: v3 adds FastText average scores of 7.09 and 5.39 in Table 2, scaling curves in Figure 7, and Turkish, threshold, and MMLU-Pro retention results. The T5 tokenizer average changes from 7.70 in v1 Table 4 to 8.11 in v3 Table 5, without a stated setting change. Original main comparison rows remain unchanged, while tokenizer-overlap results are removed.

T1.justification: Beyond v1's Bayesian decomposition and informal correspondence argument, v3 Appendix B introduces function/content-token assumptions, fixed composition ratios, and claimed noise-detection and median-threshold guarantees for mixed corpora. These are substantial new derivations, although the example for the prior mean uses unlogged probabilities inconsistently with Equation 3.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: inference-free filtering, superior average performance across 20 benchmarks, over 1000-fold speedup, and symbolic-language and multilingual applicability. The additions mainly support these existing claims.

C2.justification: Appendices B and C add explicit failure conditions for structurally plausible but meaningless text, arguments about mixed-language medians, and morpheme-based explanations of tokenizer generalization. Appendix F adds substantive arguments extrapolating small-model results to complex reasoning and interpreting MMLU-Pro retention as an indirect indicator of future performance.

D1.justification: v3 specifies that the added FastText baseline uses the same training data as DSIR and reports its filtering time. Appendix I newly describes installation, training, and testing instructions in the already-linked repository. The PDFs do not establish a new code release; the repository URL and original implementation settings remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds targeted literature supporting morphology, tokenization, experimental scale, and reasoning discussions, and expands the baseline-coverage rationale in Appendix A.2. The central positioning relative to PPL, DSIR, SCDP, and FastText remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The appendices are substantially reorganized: previously grouped tokenizer, minority-data, and sensitivity discussions become separate thematic sections. Baseline and experimental-scale explanations are expanded, and dedicated theory, generalization, reproducibility, and case sections are introduced. Much of the main narrative remains verbatim.

P2.justification: v3 adds the scaling plots and four outlier-gallery figures, restructures Table 2 with method-type and abbreviated metric columns, and splits v1's combined ablation table into separate displays. New Turkish and MMLU-Pro tables accompany extensive reflow into the conference layout; the original core figures remain.

improvement.justification: Direct FastText comparisons, larger-model and longer-training curves, and additional generalization and sensitivity tests strengthen evidence beyond v1. Explicit failure conditions also improve scope clarity. These gains are tempered by Appendix B's inconsistent treatment of the log-prior mean and Appendix F.3's unsupported extrapolation from MMLU-Pro retention to reasoning performance, limiting the overall improvement.
